newsitem.title: BELGIUM: COMMISSION SAYS RENAULT BREACHED EU DIRECTIVES.
newsitem.headline: COMMISSION SAYS RENAULT BREACHED EU DIRECTIVES.

text.p: The European Commission said on Wednesday that French car maker Renault had clearly breached European Union directives in its handling of plans to close its Belgian assembly plant.

After European Commissioners discussed the issue during their weekly meeting in Brussels, Commission chief spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas said: "The conclusion is that Renault have not respected the directives."
Plans by Renault to close itsfactory in Vilvoorde have sparked outrage in Belgium, where prospects of re-employment for over 3,000 workers are slim.

The Commission -- the EU's executive -- stressed that it was powerless to take action against Renault over the closure, but earlier implicitly suggested it was encouraging either the Belgian state or Renault workers to take legal action.
Van der Pas told Reuters that the Commissioners felt Renault was clearly in breach of two EU directives related to factory closures.
One insists companies negotiate with workers before taking a final decision on closure and the other says public authorities must be notified in advance.
Both directives have become law in France and Belgium, but the Comission said it was up to a member state or the workers to press the issue in court.
Van der Pas said the commisioners debated whether Renault's breach of the directives came about because the guidelines were not specific enough or had not been properly enforced.
"They decided it seemed it was the latter," he said. "It is a case of non-enforcement."

Van der Pas said European social affairs commissioner Padraig Flyn had nevertheless been asked by Santer to re-examine EU directives on the implications of factory closures to see if they could be strengthened.

He said Santer had also raised "on a general nature" the possibility of examining more closely whether companies were taking advantage of state or EU aid to relocate, only to move again once funds dried up.
He said, however, there was no suggestion Renault had used this tactic. -- David Fox, Brussels Newsroom ++ 32 2 287 6832
